sentences.text: Dame Agatha Mary Clarissa Christie , Lady Mallowan , DBE -LRB- née Miller ; 15 September 1890 -- 12 January 1976 -RRB- was an English crime novelist , short story writer and playwright .	DBE	Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire	crime	Crime fiction	novelist	novelist	short story writer	short story writer	playwright	playwright	Dame	Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire

She is best known for her 66 detective novels and 14 short story collections , particularly those revolving around her fictional detectives Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple .	detective	Detective fiction	Hercule Poirot	Hercule Poirot	Miss Marple	Miss Marple
She also wrote the world 's longest-running play , a murder mystery , The Mousetrap , and six romances under the name Mary Westmacott .	The Mousetrap	The Mousetrap	romances	romance novel
In 1971 she was made a Dame for her contribution to literature .	Dame	Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire
Christie was born into a wealthy upper-middle-class family in Torquay , Devon .	Torquay	Torquay	Devon	Devon

She served in a Devon hospital during the First World War , tending to troops coming back from the trenches , before marrying and starting a family in London .	Devon	Devon	First World War	First World War

She was initially an unsuccessful writer , but this all changed for the better when The Mysterious Affair at Styles was published in 1920 featuring Hercule Poirot .	Hercule Poirot	Hercule Poirot	The Mysterious Affair at Styles	The Mysterious Affair at Styles

During the Second World War she worked as a pharmacy assistant at University College Hospital , London during the Blitz and acquired a good knowledge of poisons which featured in many of her novels .	Second World War	Second World War	the Blitz	the Blitz
Guinness World Records lists Christie as the best-selling novelist of all time .	novelist	novelist	Guinness World Records	Guinness World Records

Her novels have sold roughly 2 billion copies , and her estate claims that her works come third in the rankings of the world 's most-widely published books , behind only Shakespeare 's works and the Bible .	estate	Estate (law)	Bible	Bible
According to Index Translationum , she remains the most-translated individual author -- having been translated into at least 103 languages .	Index Translationum	Index Translationum

And Then There Were None is Christie 's best-selling novel , with 100 million sales to date , making it the world 's best-selling mystery ever , and one of the best-selling books of all time .	And Then There Were None	And Then There Were None	best-selling books	List of best-selling books
Christie 's stage play The Mousetrap holds the world record for longest initial run .	The Mousetrap	The Mousetrap

It opened at the Ambassadors Theatre in the West End on 25 November 1952 and is still running after more than 25,000 performances .	Ambassadors Theatre	Ambassadors Theatre (London)	West End	West End theatre

In 1955 , Christie was the first recipient of the Mystery Writers of America 's highest honour , the Grand Master Award .	Mystery Writers of America	Mystery Writers of America	Grand Master Award	MWA Grand Master Award
Later the same year , Witness for the Prosecution received an Edgar Award by the MWA for Best Play .	Witness for the Prosecution	Witness for the Prosecution (play)	Edgar Award	Edgar Award

In 2013 , The Murder of Roger Ackroyd was voted the best crime novel ever by 600 fellow writers of the Crime Writers ' Association .	The Murder of Roger Ackroyd	The Murder of Roger Ackroyd	crime	Crime fiction

On 15 September 2015 , coinciding with her 125th birthday , And Then There Were None was named the `` World 's Favourite Christie '' in a vote sponsored by the author 's estate .	And Then There Were None	And Then There Were None	estate	Estate (law)
Most of her books and short stories have been adapted for television , radio , video games and comics , and more than thirty feature films have been based on her work .	short stories	short story
